english.html: In this error the said de Rols, supplicant, was lulled and kept for three years and more.

Great certainly was the cunning of this lecher, to keep the said de Rols in this error for three years and more, so that she infallibly believed that she was his wife. But because where there is error we say that there is no consent, nor will <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, and that evil deeds are not committed without deliberate purpose and intention to do wrong <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup> — an adultery in particular, or other kind of lechery <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup> — this woman here, as we shall discourse at length in its proper place, deserved by reason of this error some excuse. Which Pope Alexander III seems to have formally decided and determined <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>; for both the Popes and the Emperors too, in like terms, excuse the woman who remarries, thinking, with several others who also believe it, that her spouse is dead <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>, especially if the husband had remained four years or more abroad, and at the war <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>. Excused also is the virgin who marries a man already married, if she thought he was free to marry <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>. And the husband who finds his sister-in-law in his bed, and has to do with her, believing that it is his wife, is likewise excused <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. And Lot was not punished for having had to do with his two daughters, who by stealth had put themselves in his bed, because he thought he was lying with his wife <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>; nor Jacob either, going in to Leah, because he believed he had Rachel beside him. <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>

The four-year term for the wife of an absent soldier.

notes.gloss: C. 29 q. 1 treats the marriage contracted in error as to the person.
Lot and his daughters. Coras's gloss that Lot "thought he was lying with his wife" is not in the text, which says he did not perceive it.
Jacob given Leah in place of Rachel.

english.html: During which they lived as true married people, eating, drinking and sleeping ordinarily together. And of this cohabitation were begotten two children, one of whom has died.

lines: En ceſt erreur, ladite de Rols ſuppliãt,
Grande fut certeinement l'aſtuce de ce paillard, d'en-
tretenir ladite de Rols, en ceſt erreur trois ans, & dauan
tage. qu'elle infalliblement cuidoit eſtre ſa femme.
mais parce qu'où y a erreur nous diſons qu'il n'y point
de conſentement, ni de volonté {a}: & que melefices ne ſe
commettẽt point ſans propos deliberé, & intention de
malfaire {b} ſingulieremẽt vn adultere, ou autre eſpece de
paillardiſe {c}. ceſte femme ici, comme nous diſcourrons
amplement en lieu propre, meritoit pour raiſon de cet
erreur quelque excuſe. Ce que le Pape Alexãdre iij. ſem
ble auoit formellement deciz & determiné {d} car & les
Papes, & les Empereurs auſſi, en pareils termes excu-
ſent la femme qui ſe remarie: penſant auec pluſieurs au
tres, qui le cuidẽt auſſi, q̃ ſon eſpoux ſoit mort {e} meſme-
mẽt ſi le mari auoit demeuré quatre ans ou plꝰ dehors,
& à la guerre {f}. Excuſe auſſi la vierge, qui epouſe vn hõ
me ia marié, ſi elle penſoit qu'il fuſt à marier {g}. Et le
mary qui trouue ſa belleſœur dans ſon lict, & participe
auec elle, cuidant que ſoit ſa femme eſt, auſſi excuſé {h}.
Et Loth ne fut pas puni d'auoir eu affaire auec ſes deux
filles, leſquelles à la deſrobbée ſ'eſtoiẽt miſes dans ſon
lict: partant qu'il eſtimoit participer auec ſa femme {i}: ni
Iacob auſſi, ſ'approchant de Lea, par ce qu'il cuidoit a-
de ceſte cohabitation ont eſté procreez
deux enfans, l'vn deſquels eſt treſpaſſé.
